proposal: The chapter recommends repealing the tax increases from the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act (book minimum tax, stock buyback excise tax, coal excise tax, Superfund tax, drug-manufacturer excise tax) and the green-energy credits in its Subtitle D. It also recommends making the 2017 increase in the estate and gift tax exemption permanent, fully repealing the state and local tax deduction, and cutting the tax on global intangible low-taxed income to no more than 12.5 percent.

status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) made the estate and gift tax exemption permanent at $15 million, indexed, from 2026, and ended or phased out many Inflation Reduction Act energy credits: clean vehicle credits ended 2025-09-30, residential energy credits (25C and 25D) ended 2025-12-31, and wind and solar projects keep the production and investment credits only if construction begins by 2026-07-04 or they are placed in service by the end of 2027, while other credits (for example 45X, 45Q, 45U, 45Z, and credits for storage, geothermal and fuel cells) continue with new foreign-entity restrictions. The tax on global intangible income (now net CFC tested income) falls to an effective rate of about 12.6 percent, with the foreign tax credit haircut cut from 20 to 10 percent, close to the chapter's 12.5 percent ceiling. On the state and local tax deduction the Act moved opposite to the chapter in the near term, raising the cap to $40,000 for 2025 through 2029 before a permanent $10,000 cap, instead of repealing the deduction. Per the Code amendment notes, the Act did not repeal the 1 percent stock buyback excise tax and kept the corporate book minimum tax, changing only its depreciation and intangible drilling cost adjustments (section 70523).

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 enacted. The enrolled text includes Section 70106 (estate and gift exemption), Section 70120 (state and local tax limitation) and Sections 70501 to 70513 and following, which terminate or restrict clean vehicle, home energy, clean electricity production and clean electricity investment credits (section titles from the table of contents).

Law-firm summaries report: estate and gift exclusion set permanently at $15 million, indexed, for decedents dying and gifts made after 2025; state and local tax cap raised to $40,000 for 2025 through 2029, then returning to $10,000; effective global intangible low-taxed income rate about 12.6 percent for tax years beginning after 2025.
Under the Act, the clean vehicle credit (30D), previously owned clean vehicle credit (25E) and commercial clean vehicle credit (45W) end for vehicles acquired after this date.
Under the Act, the energy efficient home improvement credit (25C) and residential clean energy credit (25D) end.
Under the Act, wind and solar projects that begin construction after this date lose eligibility for the 45Y and 48E credits unless they are placed in service by the end of 2027.

title: Repeal IRA clean-energy credits and make the 2017 estate tax relief permanent
uncertainties: The official enrolled text of Title VII could not be read on govinfo because the page is cut off before it; the enacted provisions were checked through the U.S. Code amendment notes on law.cornell.edu (26 U.S.C. 2010, 164, 250, 45Y, 56A, 59A and 4501), which reproduce the Code but are not the official publication. The 12.6 percent effective rate follows from the 40 percent deduction and the 21 percent corporate rate and was not read as a stated figure. The foreign tax credit haircut change, the 25C, 25D and 30D end dates and the continuation of credits 45X, 45Q, 45U and 45Z rest on the Pierce Atwood and Ropes and Gray summaries. The coal excise tax, the Superfund tax and the drug manufacturer excise tax were not checked against the Code notes. The base erosion tax, which the same chapter page asks to eliminate, was set at 10.5 percent rather than repealed; it is outside this record's proposal. Treasury guidance on the credits issued in 2026 was not checked. The Pierce Atwood alert's publication day is approximate (July 2025).
